src.t: USGS Circular 909, Behrendt (ed.), 'Petroleum and Mineral Resources of Antarctica', 1983
SCAR Composite Gazetteer of Antarctica (AADC WFS layer SCAR_CGA_PLACE_NAMES, downloaded 2026-11-25)

sites.dt: Soviet (Ravich and others) and Australian (Tingey) geological studies, as reviewed by USGS in 1983
sites.st: Largest known iron formation in Antarctica; not economic
sites.kf: USGS Circular 909: the largest known iron-formation deposits in Antarctica are at Mount Ruker, beds up to 70 m thick in a main sequence about 400 m thick, total iron 25-46% (average 34%), phosphorus too high for good steel ore; aeromagnetic anomalies extend west for 120 km under the ice (Soviet work by Ravich and others, 1982; Australian work by Tingey).

src.t: USGS Circular 909, Behrendt (ed.), 'Petroleum and Mineral Resources of Antarctica', 1983

sites.kf: USGS Circular 909: 'In 1977, Australian geologists reported the discovery of the largest deposit of banded iron-formation in Enderby Land, at Newman Nunataks'; 750 m long, 150 m wide, 20 m thick, average 34% iron.

sites.n: Permian-Triassic coal of the Beacon Supergroup (Transantarctic Mountains; Beaver Lake, Prince Charles Mountains)

src.t: USGS Circular 909, Behrendt (ed.), 'Petroleum and Mineral Resources of Antarctica', 1983

sites.dt: Known since early expeditions; reviewed by USGS 1974 and 1983
sites.kf: USGS Circular 909: coal is widespread in Permian-Triassic rocks, with thick beds in the Beacon Supergroup of the Transantarctic Mountains and at Beaver Lake; 'None of the deposits are economically recoverable'.

sites.dt: Multichannel seismic surveys by several countries from 1976; DSDP holes in the Ross Sea, 1973
sites.st: No known petroleum resources; no drilling for petroleum
sites.kf: USGS Circular 909 (Behrendt): 'No known petroleum resources occur in Antarctica'; thick sedimentary basins have been found by seismic surveys, but there has been no offshore drilling beneath the shelf since the 1973 DSDP holes.

sites.st: Surveys continue; UK government says no evidence of drilling or extraction
sites.kf: UK FCDO written answer HL4614 (24 May 2024): Russia has a long-standing programme of surveying and mapping Antarctic geology and has assured the ATCM it is for science; 'There is no evidence of any drilling or extraction activities.'
